In detail

La Rustica is a mixed residential and light-industrial zone on Rome's eastern edge, largely low-rise housing blocks. It has a well-documented history as a base for organized drug trafficking: press reported on a local figure described as having divided Rome's drug market among associates with ties to the Mafia Capitale network, and a May 2022 police operation brought 14 arrests, including references to a 'torture room' used to enforce control over turf. Street-level dealing has drawn repeated police action too, including a 2021 sweep where residents applauded arrests from their windows. Daytime life in the area is ordinary, but the recurring, organized nature of these cases supports real caution at night.

Frequently asked questions

Is La Rustica safe?

Wandroz currently rates La Rustica in Rome as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rome during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Rome at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Rome publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is La Rustica safe at night?

At night, La Rustica is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Rome. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is La Rustica a good area to stay in as a tourist?

La Rustica's day rating (roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rome) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
